title: The derived category of modules on a ringed space has products
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and let $D(\mathcal O_X)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then every family $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ of objects of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ indexed by a set $I$ has a product $\prod_{i\in I}K_i$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-category-product]; in particular $D(\mathcal O_X)$ has countable products.

proof.text: The category of open subsets of X, with inclusions, is a small site and O_X is a sheaf of commutative rings on it. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], Mod(O_X) is Grothendieck abelian, and every complex has a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Represent each K_i by a complex and choose a K-injective resolution K_i -> I_i.

source.place: Tag 07D9, label lemma-derived-products, proof: 'choose a K-injective resolution'; Remark Tag 079Q, label remark-existence-D

proof.text: Mod(O_X) has products indexed by sets: the sectionwise product U -> prod_i F_i(U) of sheaves of O_X-modules is a sheaf of O_X-modules and is their product. Let I be the termwise product complex prod_i I_i, with projections pr_i. For any complex L, morphisms of complexes L -> I and homotopies between them are exactly families of morphisms L -> I_i and of homotopies, so Hom_{K(O_X)}(L,I) = prod_i Hom_{K(O_X)}(L,I_i) via the pr_i. If L is acyclic, every factor is 0 because each I_i is K-injective, so Hom_{K(O_X)}(L,I)=0 and I is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

source.place: Lemma Tag 070L (lemma-product-K-injective), via the Hom characterization of K-injectivity

proof.text: Let L be any complex. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied to the K-injective complexes I and I_i, and by step 2, Hom_{D(O_X)}(L,I) = Hom_{K(O_X)}(L,I) = prod_i Hom_{K(O_X)}(L,I_i) = prod_i Hom_{D(O_X)}(L,I_i) = prod_i Hom_{D(O_X)}(L,K_i), the composite bijection being composition with the images of the pr_i (and the isomorphisms I_i = K_i in D(O_X)). Hence I with these projections is a product of the family (K_i) in D(O_X) [def-weil-category-product]. Taking I countable gives the final assertion.
